source_title: The pricing of jump and diffusive risks in the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns
hypothesis: Cryptocurrencies with lower recent idiosyncratic return variance outperform higher-idiosyncratic-risk peers over the subsequent week.
mechanism: Limits to arbitrage allow low-idiosyncratic-risk crypto to earn higher subsequent returns; the source reports a low idiosyncratic diffusive risk anomaly.
market_factor: Equal-weight hourly return across contemporaneously available panel assets.
factor: Negative rolling OLS residual variance using var(asset)-cov(asset,market)^2/var(market), fully lagged by one hour.
universe: Point-in-time assets with sufficient exact hourly history and top 80 percent by lagged trailing 30-day close*volume; minimum 8 assets.
rebalance: Weekly Monday 00:00 UTC; execute at current open using statistics through prior completed hour.
construction: Equal-weight long lowest-idiosyncratic-risk tercile / short highest-idiosyncratic-risk tercile, 0.5 gross per side.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC >= 0.02, HAC p < 0.05, positive low-minus-high subsequent-week return.
limitations: This OHLCV implementation estimates total idiosyncratic variance rather than the source paper's high-frequency diffusive/jump decomposition.
